title: 1957 AHSME Problem 48
statement: Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle inscribed in circle \(O.\) \(M\) is a point on arc \(BC.\) Lines \(AM,\) \(BM,\) and \(CM\) are drawn. Then \(AM\) is:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
equal to, less than, or greater than \(BM+CM,\) depending upon
the position of \(M\)

solutions.text:
In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABMC,\) Ptolemy’s theorem gives \[ \begin{aligned} AM\cdot BC &=AB\cdot CM\\ &\quad+AC\cdot BM. \end{aligned} \] Since \(ABC\) is equilateral, \(AB=BC=AC.\) Dividing by this common length yields \[ AM=CM+BM. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Apply Ptolemy’s theorem to cyclic quadrilateral \(ABMC\)
Use \(AB=BC=CA\) to cancel the common side length
